partnershipPlan: A family partner and two rapid response team members review the interview guides; ward managers from each hospital review the safety protocol for unannounced simulation.
socialListening: No social media listening; anonymised staff comments from last year's case reviews are themed.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: Eight people arrive and three of them start the same task.
items.implication: Build role allocation into every scenario and debrief.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: For the first ten seconds I did not know if the man on the bed was a manikin or my patient.
items.implication: Use signage and a stop word, and explore ward nurse anxiety in interviews.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: They filled the room and someone told me to wait outside, and nobody came back for an hour.
items.implication: Add a family communication role to scenarios.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: I knew my mother was not right hours before anyone called the team.
items.implication: Include family concern as a trigger in ward scenarios.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: At night we are one physician for the whole hospital; your scenario must fit that.
items.implication: Design night scenarios for the staffing of the smaller hospitals.

summary: Five composite voices on roles, realism, families and small-hospital staffing.
